structuredContent.governing_intent: Create a single reviewable CANDIDATE Python engineering standard design document for the Pre-Python gate, limited to docs/architecture/pre-python-gate/python-engineering.md and local packet/readiness evidence, using cited authority and evidence without implementing Python or approving architecture.
structuredContent.summary: The work is a cohesive documentation BIU: draft a candidate design artifact that maps existing Founder-approved architecture authority, gate requirements, EOS inputs, and Node evidence into Python engineering constraints covering src layout, typing/domain immutability, async/resource discipline, configuration validation, migrations, packaging/testing, and architecture fitness checks. Intent, scope limits, authority boundaries, and acceptance signals are sufficiently specified for autonomous drafting.
implementation_unknowns: Which exact local source documents and sections correspond to the cited Authority §§33, 39, 41, EOS materials, Node evidence, and candidate conformance pins must be located and cited during drafting.
The precise packet/readiness evidence file paths and local documentation-checker invocation, if any, must be discovered from repository conventions.

How existing neighboring pre-Python candidate documents phrase cross-document references and reconciliation links must be inspected so this artifact preserves consistency without implicitly adopting them as authority.
The final set of successful and failing example scenarios must be derived from the cited constraints and checked for traceability during drafting.
independent_decision_centers: The supplied packet contains multiple design topics, but they are all subordinate to one decision center: producing one candidate Python engineering standard document under the Pre-Python gate.
structuredContent.verification_assessment: Acceptance is observable by reviewing the produced document and local packet evidence against the named rows and source authority: it should include source/invariant mapping, explicit contract semantics with passing and failing examples, scope limitations, unresolved Founder decisions if any, and clear separation between candidate design checks and future executable proof. One independent content review can provide a meaningful verdict because the expected output is a single bounded artifact with traceable source sections and no operational side effects.
material_risks: The drafter may accidentally invent or approve architecture instead of labeling material architecture/security/storage semantics as CANDIDATE for later Founder approval.
The document may prematurely fix Python package names or bounded-context names despite the authority requiring names to wait for DDD/Ubiquitous Language/bounded-context modeling.
The work may conflate historical Node behavior or EOS candidate material with Python capability proof or blanket adoption authority.
Cross-document dependencies may be adopted implicitly rather than recorded as unresolved or candidate references.
Scope creep into source, tests, configuration, service behavior, secrets, GitHub changes, or first Python implementation would violate the explicit documentation-only authorization.
structuredContent.next_action: Proceed to draft the candidate document and permitted local packet/readiness evidence, using only cited local sources, preserving CANDIDATE labeling, and validating the artifact against the stated acceptance criteria before independent review.
structuredContent.rationale: READY is the controlling disposition because the owner has provided clear governing intent, explicit scope boundaries, authorized locations, exclusions, source authority, acceptance criteria, and verification expectations. Remaining uncertainty is implementation research about locating and mapping existing materials, not unresolved owner intent. The many technical topics are coupled by a single purpose—one Python engineering standard candidate for the Pre-Python gate—so splitting would reduce coherence rather than isolate independent approval decisions. No missing external prerequisite is established by the supplied text; the packet states that needed source documents exist in named local baselines and that no new runtime regression runs are warranted for this documentation task.
